      Access

      The API key is stored on the server. Only administrators can see it, here on this page; Jellyfin never sends it to other users' browsers.

      In Seerr: Settings › General › API key. The server sends it to Seerr for search, requests and the connection test.
      hourglass_emptyNot tested

      The test asks the server to contact Seerr with the saved address and key.

        Single sign-on

        Anyone signed in to Jellyfin is signed in to Seerr too, with no login form in the frame.

        hourglass_empty…
        Can be switched on before everything below is ready; until then users get the normal Seerr sign-in.

        What it needs

          What happens when a user opens Requests

          1 · JellyfinAlready signed inNothing new to type
          2 · One-time passValid 1 minute, onceBound to that account
          3 · Quick ConnectSeerr asks JellyfinJellyfin's own sign-in check
          4 · SeerrSigned in as the same user…

          shieldNo password is bypassed. Users can only sign in as themselves, and only from the Jellyfin web client. Plain IP addresses fall back to the normal Seerr sign-in.

          expand_moreSession cookie domain (advanced)
          Leave empty: the plugin works it out from both addresses. Set it only if your setup needs a different one.
          translate

          Compatibility

          Seerr and other older apps still send their sign-in the old way. This works even when the integration is off.

          Fills in the Authorization header only when it is missing, with the same credentials and only for a single well-formed token. Never overwrites it, grants nothing extra.
          extensionSeerr sendsX-Emby-Authorizationor X-Emby-Token
